newsitem.title: USA: Apogee terminates long-term care operations.
newsitem.headline: Apogee terminates long-term care operations.

text.p: Apogee Inc said Tuesday it was terminating its long-term care operations and was consolidating a number of group practice centers in selective markets.
Most of these s most of these activities will be completed by the end of April 1997, the outpatient mental health services provider said.

As a result of these actions, it said it took a one-time charge of $14.1 million in the fourth quarter of 1996. It made the disclosures as it reported financial results for the year and fourth quarter that ended December 31.

Apogee, which operates 115 behavioral health centers in 13 states and the District of Columbia, said it has renegotiated its bank credit facility. It said that the facility, plus anticipated cash flows from operations, should be sufficient to meet the Company's projected cash requirements in the coming year.

Lawrence Davies, president and chief operating officer, said the company has completed the first phase of its stabilization of operations, eliminating parts of its business which had minimal profits but presented high risk.

He said the company was also in the process of closing, downsizing or consolidating 18 group practice centers whose performance has not met expectations, and is eliminating redundant centers in markets where the company has multiple locations.
The company has also eliminated over $1 million of corporate, regional and clinical overhead, he said.

According to the company, it has either closed, down-sized or consolidated centers in the mid-Atlantic states, Arizona, Southern California, Illinois, Southern Florida and Wisconsin to eliminate underperforming operations, over-capacity or redundancy.
It said it also withdrew from the outpatient group practice sector in Nashville, Tenn., Ft. Walton Beach, Fla., and Rhode Island markets.
